blocks.text: Guava kan spises på to stadier: modent grøn, hvor kødet er hvidt og smager som et sødt æble, eller helt moden, hvor kødet er hvidt til knaldrødt, skrællen lysegul, og frugten er meget sød og duftende.

sourceRef.locator: Guava chapter, Scientific Name and Introduction, p. 356
sourceRef.quote: The guava (Psidium guajava L.) is round or oval and can be eaten as a fresh fruit at two stages: mature green when it has white flesh and tastes like a sweet apple, or fully ripe when it has white to bright-red flesh, light-yellow skin, tastes very sweet, and is quite fragrant.

blocks.text: Grønne og halvmodne guavaer holdes ved 8–10 °C. Modne, bløde guavaer ved 5–8 °C. Luftfugtigheden bør være 90–95 %.

sourceRef.locator: Guava chapter, Optimum Storage Conditions, p. 356
sourceRef.quote: Mature green and partially ripe fruit can be held for 2 to 3 weeks at 8 to 10 °C (46 to 50 °F). Ripe, soft fruit can be held about 1 week at 5 to 8 °C (41 to 46 °F). RH of 90 to 95% is recommended

blocks.text: Umodne guavaer får kuldeskader – skjolder, fordybninger og manglende modning – og rådner lettere. Modne guavaer tåler 5 °C bedre.

sourceRef.quote: Symptoms include skin scald, pitting, and a failure to ripen if fruit are mature green or partially ripe [p367] when chilled. Browning of the flesh can occur. Decay incidence and severity increase with chilling injury. Ripe, soft fruit can be held at 5 °C (41 °F), as they are less sensitive to chilling injury.

blocks.text: Udtørring og stød er de største problemer: Skrællen bliver mat og rynket, og stødte steder bliver brune og rådner let.

sourceRef.quote: Postharvest desiccation is a major problem, along with mechanical injury. Desiccation leads to a dull yellow, sometimes wrinkled, skin, while mechanical injury leads to browning that can extend into the flesh. Mechanically injured areas of the skin and flesh are very susceptible to decay.

blocks.text: Guava danner en del ethylen (en gas, som frugt og grønt selv afgiver, og som får dem til at modne), og modningen går hurtigere, når den udsættes for ethylen.

sourceRef.locator: Guava chapter, Ethylene Production and Sensitivity, p. 357
sourceRef.quote: Production rates vary from 1 to 20 µL kg-1 h-1 at 20 °C and show a climacteric pattern of respiration. … Ripening is accelerated by exposure to ethylene

blocks.text: Grønne og halvmodne guavaer holder 2–3 uger ved 8–10 °C, modne ca. 1 uge ved 5–8 °C og ca. 7 dage ved 20 °C.

sourceRef.locator: Guava chapter, Optimum Storage Conditions, p. 356
sourceRef.quote: Mature green and partially ripe fruit can be held for 2 to 3 weeks at 8 to 10 °C (46 to 50 °F). Ripe, soft fruit can be held about 1 week at 5 to 8 °C (41 to 46 °F). … Shelf-life is about 7 days when stored at 20 °C (68 °F).
